stubs.how: The real preload (electron/preload/index.ts) is bundled into the browser build with `electron`, `os` and `@electron-toolkit/preload` aliased to small fakes (.ui-capture/web/fake-*.ts); ipcRenderer.invoke/send are routed to an in-page fake main process (.ui-capture/web/main/*.ts) that returns the same shapes as the real IPC handlers, backed by .ui-capture/web/seed.json.

stubs.service: Rust native audio engine (audio-engine via player:* IPC)
stubs.how: Silent simulated player (.ui-capture/web/main/player.ts): load/play/pause/seek/volume work and position events are pushed at 5 Hz on a wall clock; no audio output. Output devices are a fixed list (MacBook Pro speakers, AirPods Pro, FiiO K7).

Offline stand-in in .ui-capture/web/main/netease.ts: login_status reports a guest (not logged in); discover endpoints return a small set of playlists/artists/albums built from the local seed; anything else returns a 503-style 'network unavailable' error so those sections hide.

stubs.how: Handled in the fake main process: return empty/null results (lyrics not found, no comments, identity conversion).

stubs.how: Generated abstract SVG covers and avatars written by the seed generator to .ui-capture/out/covers/ and referenced as /covers/<hash>.svg.

app.notes: SPlayer-Next is an Electron app; only its Vue renderer is shown, built as a static site with `.ui-capture/build.sh` (runs the seed generator, then `vite build --config .ui-capture/web/vite.config.ts`, which reuses the renderer config from electron.vite.config.ts and only injects the browser preload shim before src/bootstrap.ts). Dependencies were installed with `.ui-capture/install.sh` (pnpm 11 because pnpm 12's store lock can't be created in this sandbox; electron-builder is dropped by .ui-capture/pnpmfile.cjs since its packages contain files the sandbox forbids and it's only for packaging). Data (generated by .ui-capture/seed/generate.mjs): a local library of 285 tracks / 44 albums / 45 artists (Chinese, Japanese and Western albums with real tracklists, FLAC + MP3, a few untagged loose files in ~/Downloads), 10 local playlists (including an empty one and a 'to sort' one), 42 liked songs, ~1600 play events over the last 8 months feeding the Stats page, 180-entry play history, a download list (done/downloading/queued/failed/canceled), and a restored play queue (playlist '深夜写代码', track 4 paused mid-song). Timestamps are shifted to the current time on load. Renderer-side state (liked ids, history, queue in IndexedDB; status in localStorage) is written through the app's own localforage stores on first open (before the app mounts). Main areas: Home (#/), Library (#/library), Liked (#/liked), History (#/history), Stats (#/stats), Folders (#/folders), Downloads (#/download), local playlists (#/collection/local/playlist/<id>), artist/album lists, search, the full-screen player, and Settings (modal).

# Running it
- Follow the repo's own setup docs and tooling. Take the simplest route that shows the real app: a static production build if the front end works without a backend, otherwise the app's own server (production or dev mode).
- If it needs a database or other services, run them locally with an embedded or file-based option (SQLite, in-memory, JSON files, an embedded Postgres such as PGlite) or the app's demo/mock mode.
- Don't redesign or restyle anything. Change only what's needed to build and run it.

# Tools: use mise
Install every runtime and tool you need (node, the package manager, python, bun, ...) with mise, pinned to exact versions in a mise.toml at the repo root, so the setup can be reproduced. Match what the repo asks for (engines, .nvmrc, .tool-versions, packageManager). mise is already configured for this directory: `mise install` installs into ./.ui-capture/mise, and its shims come first on PATH, so `node`, `pnpm` and the rest resolve to the pinned versions. Don't use other copies of these tools or download runtimes by hand.

# Secrets, API keys and external services: fake them
The app must not depend on anything outside this machine, and when it runs it has no network except localhost. Wherever it expects secrets, environment variables, API keys or third-party services (hosted auth or OAuth, payment providers, email, LLM or other AI APIs, maps, storage buckets, analytics, hosted databases):
- Give the required variables placeholder values so the app starts.
- Where it actually calls the service, make the call succeed locally with realistic responses: use the app's own mock, test or offline mode if it has one; otherwise point the client at a small local stub server that start.sh also starts, or swap in a stub at the integration boundary (the API client or service module). Keep stubs out of UI code. Responses should look like what the real service returns for a real user, e.g. an AI reply that actually answers, a payment history with real-looking amounts.
- Calls the browser makes directly to outside services count too; point them at the local stub.
- For sign-in through an outside provider, create a local account or use the app's dev sign-in so you can get past it.
List every stub in app.json.

# Data: like real use
Seed it the way an established user's data would look after months of actual use: specific, plausible names and content for this kind of app; dates spread over time; a realistic mix of states (done, in progress, overdue, archived, ...); realistic volume (dozens to hundreds of records where the app revolves around records); short and long text; some messiness real data has. Start from the app's own demo or seed data if it has realistic data, and extend it if it's thin. Load data through the app's own paths (its API, import, seed scripts, or its database schema), never by hardcoding it into UI code. If the app needs an account, create one and attach the data to it. No lorem ipsum or "Test 1".

# Environment
This shell is sandboxed: you can write only inside this directory (package-manager caches already point into ./.ui-capture/cache), and the network reaches only package registries, mise's download sources and GitHub (registry.npmjs.org, registry.yarnpkg.com, repo.yarnpkg.com, github.com, codeload.github.com, objects.githubusercontent.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, nodejs.org, mise.jdx.dev, mise-versions.jdx.dev, release-assets.githubusercontent.com, pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org, binaries.prisma.sh, cdn.jsdelivr.net, unpkg.com). Docker isn't available. A process you start in the background can't be seen or stopped from a later command, so test servers on another port than 4430 (e.g. 5430) or in the foreground under `timeout`; anything still listening on 4430 is stopped before I check.

# When you're done, leave this in ./.ui-capture/
- app.json: {"mode": "static" or "server", "entry": "/path where the main UI opens", "login": null or {"username": "...", "email": "...", "password": "..."}, "stubs": [{"service": "what was faked", "how": "how"}], "notes": "how you set it up, what data is loaded, and the main areas of the app"}
- static mode: the production build in ./.ui-capture/out, with index.html as its entry. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server; unknown paths fall back to index.html.
- server mode: ./.ui-capture/start.sh, which starts everything the app needs (stubs included) in the foreground and serves the UI at http://localhost:4430/ (it gets PORT=4430). It runs with the same PATH and restrictions as your shell, plus no network at all except localhost, so everything must already be installed, built and seeded (or seeded by start.sh itself).
- Put any scripts you write for seeding or stubbing in ./.ui-capture/ too; they're kept with the setup record.

# Order of work
You have 90 minutes in total, and anything unfinished when time runs out is lost. So work in this order:
1. Get the app building and running with its stubs, and write the contract above (app.json plus out/ or start.sh), even if it has only a little data so far.
2. Then build out the data, re-running your seed and checking the app still loads after each substantial step, so that a working state with the data loaded so far is always in place.
Write large data sets with a short generator script rather than as one long literal file.
